display.purpose: "The Lobby" on the public welcome only.

display-lead.purpose: The "Welcome to" line over the display name.

headline.purpose: The centred VIP Lobby title on navy, inside the marquee.

title.purpose: The base section-title scale; the VIP Lobby's "Your Tools" and "Admin Tools" labels run smaller (1.25rem, 650). The identity mark is a near sibling.

card-title.purpose: Tool names on VIP tiles (15ch measure); the launch screen sets the opened Tool's name in the same lettering at twice the size.

lead.purpose: Short functional sentences on the field: purpose, lead, guidance.

state.purpose: The Minecraft Launcher's server state, the biggest words in its card; Foundry's state in its status card.

value.purpose: A connection value to copy; wraps only after its dots and colons.

hint.purpose: Where a device tab plays, under its label.

shadows.name: tactile-base
shadows.purpose: Coral base and soft navy drop under every custard tactile control; --lift is 0.75rem hero, 0.5rem default, 0.3rem small.

shadows.name: tactile-base-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover and focus-visible: face lifts 2px, base deepens.

shadows.name: tactile-base-active
shadows.purpose: Pressed: face sinks onto the base.

shadows.name: ground-shadow
shadows.purpose: Soft shadow under the robot host, and the footprint under the Minecraft Launcher's server block.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The house easing (expo ease-out): state transitions, the tile rise, the launch screen, and the fallback for the selector's glide. The cabinet adds its own sampled glide and spring, and its glyph and host moves shape each keyframe with their own curves.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Hover/focus transitions on tactile and quiet controls.

motion.name: duration-press
motion.purpose: Tactile active (press) response.

motion.name: duration-arrow
motion.purpose: Hero arrow nudge on hover.

motion.name: robot-wave
motion.purpose: The host's single wave on welcome arrival, and each Minecraft transition to ready while open. Shared Tool footers are otherwise static; the VIP Lobby's host moves only with the cabinet (host-greet, host-jump).

motion.name: status-dots
motion.purpose: Checking-access loading dots, and Foundry's first check in place of its status mark.

motion.name: status-turn
motion.purpose: The busy arrow while the Minecraft Launcher's server starts or stops, or while Foundry starts or shuts down. It and the loading dots loop for as long as their wait lasts; nothing else loops, and the VIP marquee's chase is cut off by its timer.

motion.name: tool-stamp
motion.purpose: Soccer's decorative calendar check settles from scale 1.2 to 1 when a Team is selected. Disabled under reduced motion.

motion.name: glide
motion.value: --glide-tl / --glide-tr / --glide-bl / --glide-br: 480ms linear(...) per corner, sampled by cabinet.ts glide(travel, 4) (24 samples of a damped spring peaking halfway, overshoot min(4px / travel, 8%)); fallback var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: The VIP selector's per-move glide: each corner settles at most 4px past the tile however far it travels, even when a move cuts into the last one. Corners on the side it travels toward lead by up to 50ms (--lead-*).

motion.name: selector-appear
motion.value: opacity 160ms var(--ease-out); close in from 14px out, let go 7px out
motion.purpose: The selector appears by closing in on the first picked tile and lets go outward as it fades when the pointer leaves the cabinet and no tile has focus.

motion.name: spring-loose
motion.purpose: The control deck's joystick: pushed in 130ms ease-out, held 140ms, then springs back upright over 620ms with about 13% overshoot. Leans up to 22°.

motion.name: marquee-chase
motion.value: 105ms a step, 3 phases (315ms cycle), step-end; 1300ms on a pick, 2400ms on the Tools' arrival
motion.purpose: The VIP marquee's clockwise chase. Removed by its timer, so nothing loops at rest.

motion.name: marquee-flash
motion.purpose: Pressing Open flashes every marquee bulb twice; a second press switches to twin keyframes to restart it.

motion.name: deck-press
motion.value: 70ms var(--ease-out); cap sinks 3.5px and fills custard
motion.purpose: The deck's first drawn button while Open is pressed; lets up 220ms after a press that never became a click.

motion.name: tile-pick
motion.purpose: The picked VIP tile fills with limb.

motion.name: tile-rise
motion.value: 420ms var(--ease-out), 45ms stagger in reading order; from translateY(0.75rem) scale(0.96)
motion.purpose: VIP tiles rise into place as the Member's Tools arrive, fully drawn from the first frame (no fade).

motion.name: glyph-calendar
motion.value: page flips over its binding 520ms (scaleY 1 to 0.03 to 1.07 to 1); binding lifts 2px over 520ms cubic-bezier(0.3, 0.7, 0.4, 1); days pop to 1.3x over 260ms ease-out from 300ms, 40ms apart
motion.purpose: Soccer's glyph move on each pick.

motion.name: glyph-cube
motion.value: 720ms: squat, hop 5px while turning around (scaleX 1 to -1), squashed landing
motion.purpose: Minecraft Launcher's glyph move on each pick.

motion.name: glyph-foundry
motion.value: 560ms: lift 3px at 1.14x, stamp to scale(1.12, 0.84), settle
motion.purpose: Foundry's glyph move on each pick.

motion.name: glyph-gear
motion.purpose: Admin glyphs turn their gear on each pick. A glyph move already running finishes first.

motion.name: host-greet
motion.value: 620ms ease-out hop (5px, then 1.5px); arm waves 1200ms ease-in-out after 120ms
motion.purpose: The VIP footer's 40px host greets a pick, only when 12 seconds have passed since the last pick.

motion.name: host-jump
motion.value: 560ms squash-and-jump (9px); arm raises 640ms ease-in-out; restarts on each press
motion.purpose: The host jumps when Open is pressed.

motion.name: launch
motion.value: starts 90ms after the click; 560ms var(--ease-out) clip-path inset(... round 14px) from the tile's box past the screen's edges; field fill tile to seafoam; loading dots fade in 240ms after 900ms; hands the lobby back after 8000ms without a navigation
motion.purpose: The VIP launch screen grows from the opened tile while the browser loads the Tool; the link navigates at once and the screen only decorates the wait.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All CSS motion off under prefers-reduced-motion. The cabinet's scripted moves (glyph moves, marquee, joystick, host, launch) never start: the selector still marks the picked tile without travelling, and Open simply navigates.

components.description: The single primary action on the welcome: custard face, navy outline, coral base, sinks when pressed.

components.name: Marquee
components.description: 36 bulbs ring the VIP Lobby title on the navy field, 16 a row and 2 a side, numbered clockwise. Unlit bulbs are 2px seafoam rings, lit bulbs custard discs, every other one lit at rest. A pick runs a three-phase clockwise chase (105ms a step) for 1.3s, the Tools' arrival for 2.4s; Open flashes every bulb twice. Hover the sign to see the chase. Decorative and aria-hidden.

components.name: Selector
components.description: Four navy corners close around the picked tile like a game menu's cursor: 3.5px round-capped strokes on 2.25rem boxes, 8px outside the tile and concentric with its 14px corners (22px outer radius). Each corner glides 480ms on a linear() easing sampled per move so it settles at most 4px past the tile; it appears by closing in from 14px further out. Hover the tile to see it close in.

components.name: Control Deck
components.description: A seafoam ledge 3.5 to 4.25rem tall under the VIP cabinet, drawn in the glyph stroke: a navy ball-top joystick on a pale washer that leans up to 22° toward each move and springs back (620ms, --spring-loose, about 13% overshoot), and two buttons with navy housings and pale caps that are drawn, never pressable; the first sinks 3.5px and lights custard when Open is pressed. Hover leans the stick; press shows the lit button. Decorative and aria-hidden.

narrative.overview:
The Lobby looks like the title screen of a friendly couch co-op game: a matte seafoam field, deep navy lettering and outlines, and one fat custard button sitting on a coral base, waiting to be pressed. Everything is drawn as flat, outlined shapes in a small palette, the way a cartoon game menu is drawn, and the depth that exists is physical (a button you press down) rather than atmospheric.

The public welcome is a single title menu with giant centred lettering, one action, a low custard sun, and layered seafoam foliage. A small robot host waves once beside the navy ground wave. The signed-in VIP Lobby uses **Arcade Cabinet**, selected by Craig on 2026-11-11, and **Attract Mode**, chosen the same day to bring it to life. The title is centred inside a marquee of bulbs on the navy field above a pale seafoam cabinet. Each seafoam Tool tile acts as a launch key, with a navy glyph, a full Tool name, and a custard Open control. Picking a tile closes a navy selector around it and plays its glyph's move; pressing Open grows the tile into a launch screen while the Tool loads. A seafoam control deck with a joystick and two buttons sits under the cabinet. The launcher keeps the robot at 40px in its navy footer.

Tool interiors share a blocky world drawn in those same materials: isometric miniatures, navy number tiles, framed controls and a stepped navy ground. Minecraft has its server block, Soccer a pitch and calendar, and Foundry a tabletop scene. Each drawing belongs to its task and leaves the working controls in reach.

Navy does every structural job (type, outlines, rules, glyphs, focus rings, the ground). Custard is the action and drawn light (the welcome's sun, the server block's lamp). Coral is the tactile base and the robot's body, never text. Seafoam and its lighter tints are the field and the surfaces.
keyCharacteristics: Matte seafoam field with navy type and navy outlines on everything drawn.
One tactile control: custard face, navy outline, coral base, sinks when pressed.
Rounded, chunky lettering (Rubik) over a soft, readable text face (Nunito Sans).
Flat surfaces separated by 2px navy outlines and 1.5px navy rules, not by shadow.
Hand-drawn SVG scenery and a robot host, all in the token palette, all decorative.
One task-specific miniature per Tool interior, drawn in the Lobby's own block materials, with shared number tiles and stepped ground.

rules.name: The Navy Does the Drawing Rule
rules.body: Outlines, rules and glyph strokes stay navy. Text and focus rings are navy on light surfaces; on navy regions, text flips to seafoam-light with seafoam supporting copy, footer links and focus rings turn custard.

rules.name: The One Thing to Press Rule
rules.body: Custard on a coral base means "press me". Do not use custard as a surface fill for cards, panels or banners, and do not use coral for anything that is not a tactile base or the robot. Outside the tactile control, custard appears only as drawn light: the welcome's sun, the server and tabletop lamps, the VIP marquee's lit bulbs, and the control deck's first button while Open is pressed. The deck's buttons are drawn, never pressable, so they stay pale at rest.

rules.name: The Heavy Menu Rule
rules.body: Headings run tight (negative tracking from -0.005em to -0.025em, line-height at or under 1.05) and balanced. Body text never goes tight.

rules.name: The Semibold Voice Rule
rules.body: Short functional sentences on the field (purpose, lead, guidance, notices, status) are Nunito Sans 600, so they hold up on saturated seafoam. Long running text stays at 400.

rules.name: The Only Pressable Thing Has Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth means "this can be pressed". Cards, panels, notices and the quiet button stay flat; the coral base and its lift belong to the tactile control alone.

dos: **Do** draw every line, letter, outline and glyph in navy; flip to seafoam-light text and custard links and focus rings on the navy ground.
**Do** make the primary action the custard tactile control with its coral base, and keep one per view at hero size.
**Do** separate cards and panels with 2px navy outlines on 1rem corners, and page regions with 1.5px navy rules.
**Do** draw new Tool glyphs in the existing stroke family: 32px grid, 2.5px navy stroke, round joins; admin variants add the corner gear.

**Do** keep sun, foliage and ground wave on the public welcome. Give Tool interiors their shared block world and task-specific miniature. Keep every illustration and the robot decorative and aria-hidden.

**Do** give a copy action the custard face once copying is the job of the moment, and drop every other control in view to quiet. On the Launcher each ready world's Copy address and each stopped world's Start are their own job, so each takes the custard face.
**Do** honour reduced motion: every animation and transition is switched off under prefers-reduced-motion.
**Do** keep the VIP cabinet's motion answering the Member (the Tools arriving, a pick, a press) and settling within a few seconds; nothing moves at rest.
donts: **Don't** give cards, panels, notices or the quiet button a shadow or a coral base; depth belongs to the pressable control.
**Don't** set text in coral or custard on the seafoam field.
**Don't** fill cards or banners with custard; custard is the action and drawn light (the sun, the server and tabletop lamps, the VIP marquee's bulbs and the deck's pressed button).
**Don't** introduce a second line colour, gradients, or backdrop-blur glass; the world is matte and flat-drawn (the welcome's faint print grain is the only texture).
**Don't** borrow Minecraft's own art for the block motif: no logo, textures, grass or dirt colours, block faces, hard offset "block" shadows or pixel fonts.
**Don't** use colour alone or a custard surface to say a server's state; the state is said in words, with a drawn glyph beside them.
**Don't** give the control deck's drawn buttons a custard face at rest, or anything to do; the custard Open control is the one thing to press.
